text: I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any fevers, night sweats, or pain in your joints recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient reports a 6-month history of fatigue and an unintentional weight loss of 5 kg (11 lb) despite maintaining a good appetite. He denies any recent changes in his diet or physical activity. He takes no medications and does not smoke or use illicit drugs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any shortness of breath, chronic cough, or abdominal pain? Have you noticed any swelling in your abdomen or changes in your bowel habits?

text: Do you have a history of diabetes or thyroid disease, and have you noticed any palpitations or heat intolerance? I would also like to examine your abdomen for any organ enlargement or masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see your white blood cell count is elevated and you have anemia, but your liver tests and ultrasound are normal. Have you noticed any new lumps or swelling in your neck, armpits, or groin, or any unexplained bruising or bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, night sweats, changes in bowel or bladder habits, recent infections, or bleeding disorders.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the elevated white blood cell count and anemia with a normal abdominal ultrasound, I need to rule out hematologic malignancies. Have you noticed any enlargement of your spleen or liver, or any bone pain? REQUEST TEST: Peripheral_Smear

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Peripheral_Blood_Smear: Increased lymphocytes with smudge cells

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of smudge cells on the peripheral smear, combined with lymphocytosis and anemia in an elderly patient, is highly characteristic of Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)
